Adding detail on the Dedicated timeline exception.

Summary: The autoscale work depends on a kernel selection change and additional perf testing. Current estimate shifts from 2026-11-15 to ~2026-12-06 (3 weeks). Root causes: additional hardware variance found in nightly perf tests; safety gates require one extra regression run.

Mitigation options (quick):
- Option A: Prioritize a limited autoscale subset (short sequences only) to ship by 2026-11-20, full scope 2026-12-06. Tradeoff: reduced throughput for long-seq jobs.
- Option B: Keep full scope but accept the slip; offer an interim throughput SLA for impacted customers (requires product + sales to craft wording).

I'll prepare a one-page exception note and mitigation matrix. Attaching a short draft: Dedicated-Timeline-exception.md

— Markus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Looping Emma for visibility — Greenline procurement has explicitly asked for a higher-availability SLA option tied to Dedicated (they're one of the enterprise pilots). Their procurement team wants proposed language on credits, and they want to understand tradeoffs if autoscale is delayed. Emma, CC'd, can you confirm whether Greenline expects formal acceptance before QBR?

From the sales side, options that look realistic to me:
- Offer a 'Defined Peak SLA' for long-seq jobs with a higher credit (short-term interim)
- Or provide a roadmap commitment + a conditional credit that scales down if the autoscale slip is delivered within a defined window

I'll draft two language options by 2026-10-07 EOD and post to the tracker. HubSpot: HS-28941 has the procurement thread.
